# 2 Baruch Chapter 48 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Fourth Fast and Dialogue

---

**1** After all this, I prayed: "O Lord, you who called into existence what did not exist, who brings down what has not yet arrived, and who reveals what is hidden —

**2** you who sustain life by your power, decree death by your will, and make suffering known by your counsel.

**3** You measured the sky by a hand's span and the dust of the earth in a jar; you weighed the mountains on a scale and the hills in a balance.

**4** You spread out the heavens like a curtain and set the earth firm upon the waters.

**5** You brought forth springs of fire and dark waters beneath the sky, and positioned the fountains of the deep in their places.

**6** By your word you enclosed the sea, by your power you restrained the deep, and by your wisdom you dried up the great primordial waters.

**7** By your word you created humanity and ordered all human generations by your wisdom.

**8** The depths of the abyss and the hidden chambers of the earth lie open to you, and the realm of the dead is under your authority.

**9** You know before they arrive what the coming years will bring, and what each passing year contains.

**10** Your kingdom lasts forever, and no one can put a limit on your glory.

**11** Before your greatness the angelic hosts tremble, and all the fiery beings serve your glory.

**12** Fire and hail obey your decrees; snow and frost carry out your commands.

**13** You set apart for yourself a people from all the nations — a people called your firstborn, your only-begotten, your beloved.

**14** You made a covenant with our father Abraham, swore an oath to Isaac, and confirmed it with Jacob.

**15** You brought your people out of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, and led them through the wilderness.

**16** You fed them with manna and gave them water from the rock, and sheltered them under the cloud's shadow by day.

**17** You gave them your law, placed righteousness before them, and established with them the covenant of life.

**18** You gave them commandments and statutes and laid before them the way of life and the way of death.

**19** Hear my prayer now, O Lord! You have never shut yourself off from your people's cries.

**20** "You know what we have done. Our ancestors disobeyed you, and now you have punished us as our ways deserved.

**21** Do not hold our ancestors' sins against us — instead, remember your power and your name at this moment.

**22** We have sinned and broken your statutes. You are righteous, O Lord our God.

**23** But do not wipe us out as you would nations that have never known you. Do not treat us like peoples who have never called on your name.

**24** Every nation has sinned against you, and they are all without understanding. But among us, your own people, there is knowledge — though it may be imperfect.

**25** "I know you are angry with us, yet you have not destroyed us completely — because we are the people on whom you have placed your mercy.

**26** Did you not divide the world among Adam's descendants? Did you not reveal to them the ways of your wisdom?

**27** Did you not plant in them the seed of eternal life and show them the paths of correction?

**28** You gave them the foundation of wisdom and the grasp of truth.

**29** You promised them life and warned them of death, and at the end of time you will judge them.

**30** "So now, turn your mercy toward us. We are the people who have called on your name.

**31** Yes, we have sinned — but we have accepted your discipline. And those who scattered us will not last forever.

**32** Think about the nations that do not know you, who live as if there is no judgment coming.

**33** You know every secret in the world, everything buried beneath the earth, every thought in every human heart.

**34** You know how time ends and the day when everything will stand revealed before you.

**35** You know the count of all births and all deaths yet to come.

**36** You know how many will die in fire or water, how many will fall by the sword, and how many will go into captivity.

**37** You know how many will be devoured by wild animals or worms, and how many will die in plagues.

**38** And you know whether the end of the age will come with great violence or in quiet stillness.

**39** "O Lord my God, you alone know the full depth of your wisdom and the vast breadth of your understanding. No one can grasp the thinking of your mind.

**40** Truly, even the heavens cannot contain you — how much less these buildings that human hands have made!

**41** Yet you chose this people and called this land holy, and you made this the dwelling place of your name.

**42** And now you have let the nations trample it, and those who hate us have gotten the upper hand.

**43** Our enemies mock us, and those who despise us celebrate our ruin.

**44** What is going to become of your name, O Lord? What will the nations say about your glory?

**45** Are you not the one who promised Zion would be restored? Are you not the one who said your people would be brought back together?

**46** But now we are scattered, our enemies are winning, and no one is helping us.

**47** "Do not forget your servants, O Lord. We did not abandon your law by choice — we were taken captive against our will.

**48** Even while scattered among the nations, we kept your law through all our suffering.

**49** Now, O Lord, look at us and show us grace. You are our only hope. There is no rescue for us apart from you.

**50** If you show us no mercy, nothing can save us. If you do not gather us, we will perish."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Prioritizes clarity and natural English flow while preserving the theological and narrative content of the Syriac source.*
